L2t: A promise to pay a debt barred by the statute of limitations is generally treated as enforceable without new consideration under the moral-obligation doctrine, but many jurisdictions add formal requirements for it.
L3t: The promise to pay a time-barred debt is enforceable only if it satisfies the formalities, and since this promise was only oral and the question asks for the strongest ground of unenforceability, the formality rule is what matters, not the lapse of the limitations period.
L4t: The oral promise is unenforceable because it violates the statute of frauds, which requires a promise to pay a time-barred debt to be in writing.
L2f: Statutes of limitations on contract debts commonly run for many years, and the length of the period varies widely from state to state.
L3f: Because the limitations period had already expired on July 1, the debt was extinguished completely, and a later promise cannot revive a claim that has been legally wiped out.
L4f: The strongest ground is that the debt was already barred by the statute of limitations, so the oral promise cannot be enforced.
cand_true: Violates the statute of frauds (promise not in writing)
cand_wrong1: Debt was barred by the statute of limitations
cand_wrong2: Lack of consideration for the promise
